## Step 5: Mapping Planning
-**Status**: NOT STARTED
+**Status**: COMPLETE
+### Session definition
+One converted session = one of the **89 recordings**. Behaviour for a recording is taken from
+the *first* experiment type that contains it (they are identical); `stim_id` is merged over
+**all** experiment types containing it.
+### Timepoint selection (per recording)
+nfr   = spk.shape[1]                        # reference: load_spk / Get_dprime_selective_neuron
+keep  = (ft_move[:nfr] > 0) & ft_CorrSpc[:nfr] & ~isnan(ft_trInd[:nfr])
+Trial t = the retained frames with `ft_trInd == t`, in time order. Median 22 frames/trial.
### Variable Mapping
| Source Variable | Target Field | Transform | Reference Code Function(s) | Notes |

+| `spks` (list of 3 plane arrays) | `neural` | concat along neurons → keep visual-area neurons → keep retained frames → z-score per neuron → subsample 2000 neurons → split by trial | `load_spk`, `Get_dprime_selective_neuron` (`fr_valid`) | float32, (n_neurons, T_trial) |
+| `iarea` (retinotopy) | `brain_region_idx` | `neu_area_ID` mapping to `['V1','mHV','lHV','aHV']`; drop `iarea ∈ {−1,7}` | `neu_area_ID`, `Get_density_map` | |
+| `SoundTime`, `ft` | `input[0]` "time_to_sound_cue_s" | `(SoundTime[trial] − ft[t]) × 86400`, clipped to ±30 s | `beh['SoundTime']` | continuous, time-varying; >0 before the cue |
+| `datexp` | `input[1]` "day_of_training" | days since that mouse's **first** recording | `Imaging_Exp_info` | continuous, per-trial (broadcast over time) |
+| `Trial_start_time`, `ft` | `input[2]` "time_since_trial_start_s" | `(ft[t] − Trial_start_time[trial]) × 86400`, clipped to 30 s | `beh['Trial_start_time']` | continuous, time-varying |
+| `WallName`, `isRew` | `input[3]` "reward_available" | `1` if `WallName[trial] == WallName[isRew][0]`, else `0`; all-0 for sessions with no rewards | `get_cat_id` | discrete, per-trial |
+| `WallName` + merged `stim_id` | `output[0]` "stimulus" | canonical role id 0–6, plus 7 for `circle3` | `Get_coding_direction` docstring, `get_cat_id` | per-trial (broadcast) |
+| `LickFr` | `output[1]` "licking" | `1` for frames `floor(LickFr)`, else 0 | `spk_2_firstLick` (`beh['LickFr'].astype(int)`) | binary, time-varying |
+| `ft_Pos` | `output[2]` "position_bin" | `floor(ft_Pos/10)` clipped to 0–3 → 4 bins of 1 m over 0–4 m | corridor geometry (`Texture_Length=40` dm) | time-varying |
+| `ft_RunSpeed` | `output[3]` "running_speed_bin" | quartile bin (0–3) using **global** quartiles over all retained timepoints | Methods "Running speed" | time-varying |
+| `mname` | `subjects` / `subject_idx` | 19 unique | | |
### Key Decisions
+1. **All 89 recordings / 19 mice are kept.** The paper analyses all of them; no session-level
+   quality criterion exists in code or text.
+2. **Timepoints: `(ft_move>0) & ft_CorrSpc`.** Identical to `fr_valid` in
+   `Get_dprime_selective_neuron` and to the Methods ("0–4 m region", "excluded the data points
+   in which the animal was not running"). It also removes the reward-collection stops, exactly
+   as the paper intends.
+3. **Native imaging frames as time bins** (314.7 ms; frame rate varies by <0.4 % across
+   sessions, so a single `time_bin_size` is reported). No re-binning — the imaging rate is
+   already slow, and the paper's only re-binning is onto position, which cannot be used when
+   position is a decoder target.
+4. **Neurons: visual-cortex only (`iarea ∉ {−1,7}`), then a seeded random subsample of up to
+   2000 per session, stratified proportionally over V1/mHV/lHV/aHV.**
+   Rationale: 4.1 M visual neurons × 821 k timepoints is ~150 GB and would make both the pickle
+   and the 200-epoch decoder training intractable (every epoch copies the whole dataset to the
+   GPU). 2000 is exactly `decoder.train_decoder`'s `svd_max_neurons` default, so the SVD
+   initialisation is computed on the true neurons rather than on a random Gaussian projection.
+   Stratifying keeps each session's area composition. Seeded → reproducible.
+5. **Neural activity is z-scored per neuron** over the retained timepoints of its session.
+   Deconvolved Suite2p amplitudes are in arbitrary, wildly heterogeneous units (per-neuron s.d.
+   spans 0.5 – 350 within one session; values up to 2849). The decoder initialises its
+   projection with an **uncentred** SVD and then feeds the projections straight into a linear
+   layer at lr = 1e-3, so raw amplitudes produce saturated logits. Z-scoring makes the SVD a
+   true PCA and is the standard preprocessing for deconvolved traces in this lab's pipelines.
+   This is the one deliberate deviation from the reference, required by "training a neural
+   decoder"; it is a per-neuron affine rescaling and therefore changes no relative structure.
+6. **Reward availability = rewarded *corridor*, not reward delivered** (see Step 4). Prevents
+   leaking the licking output into the decoder input.
+7. **Stimulus = canonical role id** (0 circle1, 1 circle2, 2 leaf1, 3 leaf2, 4 leaf3,
+   5 leaf1_swap1, 6 leaf1_swap2, 7 circle3). Pools rock/brick mice onto the leaf/circle roles
+   exactly as the paper does, giving one label set that means the same thing in every session.
+8. **Time inputs clipped to ±30 s.** Wall-clock time is used (not "running time"), because that
+   is the true time since corridor entry and because running-frame counts would make position
+   a deterministic function of the input. ~2 % of retained samples come from trials in which the
+   mouse paused for tens of seconds inside the corridor (max 400 s); clipping keeps the linear
+   decoder well conditioned without discarding any data.
+9. **Running-speed bins from global quartiles** — the spec says each bin should hold 25 % of
+   the data, which is only exactly true if the quantiles are computed over the pooled dataset.
+10. **No trials are dropped.** Every one of the 38,110 trials has ≥1 retained frame (verified).
### Planned Sanity Checks
+- [ ] 89 sessions, 19 mice, 38,110 trials, 821,579 timepoints in the converted file.

# Dataset Conversion Notes

## Overview
- **Dataset**: Zhong, Baptista, Gattoni, Arnold, Flickinger, Stringer & Pachitariu,
  *"Unsupervised pretraining in biological neural networks"* (`/app/paper.pdf`).
  Two-photon mesoscope calcium imaging of mouse visual cortex during a virtual-reality
  visual-discrimination task. Figshare DOI 10.25378/janelia.28811129.v1
- **Date started**: 2026-09-19
- **Goal**: Convert to decoder-compatible format (`/app/converted_data.pkl`)

---

## Step 0: Setup and Initialization
**Status**: COMPLETE

Environment verified: `numpy 2.4.4`, `torch 2.6.0+cu124`, `scipy 1.18.0`, `h5py 3.16.0`.
Hardware: 1006 GB RAM, 128 CPUs, 1x NVIDIA L4 (23 GB).

Directory contents of `/app`:
- `.manifest`, `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yaml`
- `CONVERSION_NOTES.md` (this file)
- `paper.pdf` (25 pages), `methods.txt` (excerpt of paper methods)
- `decoder.py` (89 KB, decoder library), `train_decoder.py` (validation/training driver)
- `code/` — reference code from the paper:
  `README.md`, `LICENSE`, `utils.py` (947 lines), `data_process_script.ipynb`,
  `Figures.ipynb`, `fig1.py`, `fig2.py`, `fig3.py`, `fig4.py`, `fig5.py`, `S6.py`
- `data/`
  - `data/beh/` (6.6 GB): 23 `Beh_<exp_type>.npy` files, `Imaging_Exp_info.npy`,
    `example_bef_and_aft_learning_behavior.npy`, `Unsupervised_pretraining_behavior/` (3 files)
  - `data/spk/` (405 GB): 89 `<mouse>_<date>_<blk>_neural_data.npy` files
  - `data/retinotopy/` (170 MB): 89 `<mouse>_<date>_trans.npz` + `areas.npz`
  - `data/process_data/` (empty — intermediate results are regenerated by the reference notebook)

---

## Step 1: Reference Code Exploration
**Status**: COMPLETE

### Key Functions Identified

| Function | File | Stage | Purpose |
|----------|------|-------|---------|
| `download_data_from_figshare` | utils.py:12 | LOADING | Downloads `spk/`, `beh/`, `retinotopy/` from Figshare; defines the directory layout |
| `load_exp_beh(root, exp_type)` | utils.py:326 | LOADING | `np.load('beh/Beh_<exp_type>.npy').item()` → dict keyed by `<mname>_<datexp>_<blk>[_<stimtype>]` |
| `load_spk(db, root)` | utils.py:338 | LOADING | `np.concatenate(np.load('<mname>_<datexp>_<blk>_neural_data.npy').item()['spks'], 0)` → (n_neurons, n_frames) deconvolved traces |
| `load_retino(db, root)` | utils.py:330 | LOADING | Loads `<mname>_<datexp>_trans.npz`; returns `xy_t`, `iarea`, and `neu_ar_idx` (per-area boolean masks) |
| `neu_area_ID(iarea)` | utils.py:312 | CURATION | Maps `iarea` code → visual area: **V1** = 8; **mHV** = 0,1,2,9; **lHV** = 5,6; **aHV** = 3,4. Codes −1 and 7 are *not* in any area |
| `Get_dprime_selective_neuron` | utils.py:418 | PROCESSING | Canonical frame-selection recipe: `fr_valid = (ft_move[:nfr] > 0) & ft_CorrSpc[:nfr]` — "only use activity inside the texture area plus mouse is running (VR moving)" |
| `Get_density_map` | utils.py:394 | CURATION | `idx_neu = (iarea != -1) & (iarea != 7)` — "exclude neurons from outside of visual cortex" |
| `dprime(x1, x2)` | utils.py:370 | PROCESSING | `2*(µ1−µ2)/(σ1+σ2)` on raw deconvolved traces |
| `spk_pos_interp` / `get_interpPos_spk` | utils.py:105/120 | PROCESSING | Interpolates activity onto 60 position bins per trial (1 dm each, 6 m of VR). Used for the paper's position-tuning figures only |
| `get_cat_id(WallName, isRew)` | utils.py:137 | PROCESSING | Assigns canonical stimulus roles from the *rewarded* wall: rewarded stim → 2, its "2" variant → 3, other stim → 0, its "2" variant → 1 |
| `get_lick_raster`, `lick_response` | utils.py:149/238 | PROCESSING | Behavioural lick analyses; use `LickPos`/`LickTrind` |
| `spk_2_firstLick`, `spk_2_cue` | utils.py:913/935 | PROCESSING | Event-aligned activity; **uses `beh['LickFr'].astype(int)` and `beh['SoundFr'].astype(int)`** — i.e. event frame indices are *truncated* (floor) to the containing imaging frame |
| `data_process_script.ipynb` cell 9 | code/ | PROCESSING | Top-level loop: `VRmove = beh['ft_move'][:nfr] > 0`, `ft_AcumPos = beh['ft_PosCum'][:nfr]`, then position interpolation with `n_bins=60, lengths=Corridor_Length` |

### Notes
- Neural data are **deconvolved** Suite2p traces (`spks`), stored as a list of 3 sub-arrays
  (imaging planes/slices) that are concatenated along the neuron axis. No ΔF/F needs to be
  computed — the paper states "All our analyses were based on deconvolved fluorescence traces".
- No spike-sorting quality filtering exists (this is imaging, not ephys). Suite2p's own cell
  classifier has already been applied upstream. The only neuron curation in the reference code
  is **anatomical**: keep neurons assigned to a visual area (`iarea ∉ {−1, 7}`).
- The reference code **truncates behaviour to the number of neural frames**: `nfr = spk.shape[1]`,
  then `beh['ft_*'][:nfr]`. The behaviour arrays are 1 frame longer than the imaging arrays.
- The reference never normalises `spks` before analysis (it uses d′, which is scale-free).
- `data_process_script.ipynb` documents every `beh` field (copied into Step 2 below).

---

## Step 2: Dataset Exploration
**Status**: COMPLETE

### Data Structure

**`data/beh/Imaging_Exp_info.npy`** → dict with 23 *experiment types* (keys):
`unsup_train1_before_learning`, `unsup_train1_after_learning`, `sup_train1_before_learning`,
`sup_train1_after_learning`, `unsup_test1`, `sup_test1`, `naive_test1`, `unsup_test2`,
`sup_test2`, `naive_test2`, `unsup_test3`, `sup_test3`, `naive_test3`,
`unsup_train2_before_learning`, `sup_train2_before_learning`, `unsup_train2_after_learning`,
`sup_train2_after_learning`, `train1_before_grating`, `train1_after_grating`,
`test1_before_grating`, `test1_after_grating`, `test2_before_grating`, `test2_after_grating`.

Each value is a list of "db" dicts: `mname`, `datexp`, `blk`, optional `stimtype`
(`swap1`/`swap2`), `exptype` (`sup`/`unsup`/`naive`/absent), `rewType`, `stim_id`
(canonical id for each entry of `UniqWalls`, `NaN` where not used in that comparison), etc.
**142 db entries → 89 unique recordings** (a recording can appear under several experiment
types, e.g. a `test1` session is also the `train2_before_learning` session).

**`data/beh/Beh_<exp_type>.npy`** → dict keyed `<mname>_<datexp>_<blk>[_<stimtype>]`. All entries
for the same recording carry identical behaviour (same `ntrials`, same `ft`); they differ only
in the `stim_id` labelling supplied by `Imaging_Exp_info`.

Behaviour fields used here (definitions from `data_process_script.ipynb`):

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ntrials` | number of corridor traversals |
| `Corridor_Length` = 60, `Texture_Length` = 40, `Gray_Space_length` = 20 | in **decimetres**: 4 m of texture + 2 m of grey |
| `ft` (n_frames,) | MATLAB datenum timestamp of each **imaging frame** |
| `ft_trInd` | trial index of each frame (NaN outside behaviour) |
| `ft_Pos`, `ft_PosCum` | position in VR (dm) per frame; cumulative |
| `ft_move` | `diff(ft_PosCum)` — >0 iff the VR advanced during that frame |
| `ft_CorrSpc`, `ft_GraySpc` | in texture area (`ft_Pos < 40`) / in grey (`ft_Pos ≥ 40`) — verified exactly |
| `ft_RunSpeed` (= `RunFr` up to a constant scale) | ball running speed interpolated to imaging frames (cm s⁻¹) |
| `ft_WallID` | stimulus name of the corridor each frame belongs to |
| `Trial_start_time`, `Trial_end_time`, `Gray_space_time` | wall-clock times of corridor entry / exit / grey entry |
| `StartFr`, `GrayFr`, `EndFr`, `SoundFr`, `SoundDelayFr`, `RewardFr`, `LickFr` | (fractional) imaging-frame indices of the same events |
| `SoundTime`, `SoundTimeDelay`, `SoundPos` | time / position of the sound cue (per trial) |
| `RewTime`, `RewPos`, `isRew` | reward delivery time/position; `isRew` = reward **was delivered** |
| `WallName`, `UniqWalls`, `stim_id` | stimulus per trial / unique stimuli / canonical ids |
| `LickTime`, `LickPos`, `LickTrind`, `LickFr` | one entry per lick |

**`data/spk/<mname>_<datexp>_<blk>_neural_data.npy`** → `{'spks': [3 float32 arrays]}`, each
`(n_neurons_plane, n_frames)`; concatenated along axis 0 gives `(n_neurons, n_frames)`
deconvolved activity. `n_frames` = `len(ft) − 1` in the sessions checked.

**`data/retinotopy/<mname>_<datexp>_trans.npz`** → `xy_t` (n_neurons, 2) cortical coordinates,
`iarea` (n_neurons,) area code, `xpos`, `ypos`, `A`. `len(iarea)` equals the concatenated
neuron count of the matching `spk` file (verified). `areas.npz` holds the 10 area outlines.

### Dataset Size (from data files)
| Statistic | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Subjects (mice) | **19** (`DR10, DR15, LZ13, LZ16, TX104, TX105, TX108, TX109, TX119, TX123, TX124, TX139, TX140, TX60, TX61, TX83, TX85, TX88, VR2`) |
| Sessions (recordings) | **89** (89 spk files ↔ 89 unique `Imaging_Exp_info` recordings, exact match) |
| Sessions / subject | 1–8 (mean 4.7) |
| Neurons (total, all recorded) | 4,691,034 (mean 52,708 / session; **min 20,547, max 89,577**) |
| Neurons in a visual area (`iarea ∉ {−1,7}`) | 4,105,393 (mean 46,128; min 17,363, max 78,815) |
| Trials (total) | **38,110** (mean 428 / session; range 84–789) |
| Imaging frame rate | 3.171–3.181 Hz across sessions (median **3.1777 Hz** → 314.7 ms bin) |
| Timepoints in corridor while VR moving | **821,579** (mean 9,231 / session; median 22 frames / trial) |
| Trials in a rewarded corridor | 4,446 / 38,110 = 11.7 % (28 sessions from 5 task mice) |

Stimulus (`WallName`) counts over all 38,110 trials:
`leaf1 9736, circle1 9393, leaf2 4841, rock1 2743, wood1 2517, circle2 1836, wood2 1592,
leaf3 1545, leaf1_swap2 821, leaf1_swap1 818, wood5 567, rock2 535, wood1_swap2 421,
circle3 390, wood1_swap1 355`.

---

## Step 3: Reference Text Reading
**Status**: COMPLETE

### Expected Statistics (from paper/methods)
| Statistic | Value | Source Quote |
|-----------|-------|--------------|
| Recordings | 89 | "We performed 89 recordings in 19 mice" |
| Subjects | 19 | same |
| Neurons / recording | 20,547 – 89,577 | "activity traces from 20,547 to 89,577 neurons in each recording" |
| Corridor geometry | 4 m corridor + 2 m grey | "The virtual reality corridors were each 4 m long, with 2 m of grey space between corridors" |
| VR speed | 60 cm s⁻¹ (constant while running) | "the virtual corridors always moved at a constant speed (60 cm s−1)" |
| Running threshold | 6 cm s⁻¹ for ≥66 ms | "running faster than a threshold of 6 cm s−1"; "faster than 6 cm s−1 for at least 66 ms (a threshold that triggers the motion of the virtual reality)" |
| Sound-cue position | uniform 0.5 – 3.5 m | "the time of the sound cue was randomly chosen per trial from a uniform distribution between positions 0.5 m and 3.5 m" (data: 0.4 – 3.9 m) |
| Neural signal | deconvolved Suite2p traces, τ_decay = 0.75 s | "For non-negative deconvolution, we used a timescale of decay of 0.75 s. All our analyses were based on deconvolved fluorescence traces" |
| Calcium frame rate | 3.17 Hz | `data_process_script.ipynb`: "Calcium signal recording frame rate: fs = 3.17Hz" |
| Analysis window | 0–4 m of the corridor | "we only selected data points inside the 0–4-m region of the corridors where the textures were shown" |
| Data exclusion | non-running timepoints removed | "We excluded the data points in which the animal was not running, so that all data points included ... came from similar engagement or arousal levels"; "We only considered timepoints during running for analysis, which removed time periods when the task mice stopped to collect water rewards" |
| Selective-neuron criterion (paper analyses only) | d′ ≥ 0.3 | "The criteria for selective neurons was d′ ≥ 0.3" |
| Brain regions | V1, medial HV, lateral HV, anterior HV | Figs. 1j, 2i, 3 use `['V1','mHV','lHV','aHV']` |
| Cohorts | 5 task (sup) mice, 7–9 unsupervised, 9 naive (11 sessions), VRg gratings mice | Fig. 3/Ext. Data Fig. 3 legends |
| Reward rate | rewarded corridor is 1 of the 2 trained corridors (≈50 % of trials in task sessions) | "For task mice, the sound cue indicated the beginning of the reward zone in the rewarded corridor" |
| Stimulus naming | leaf/circle (also rock/brick in some mice) | "we denote the stimuli as 'leaf' and 'circle', even though other visual stimuli were also used in some mice ('rock' and 'bricks')" |

### Processing Details
- Temporal alignment for the decoder task: **trial start = corridor entry**
  (`Trial_start_time`, i.e. the frame at which `ft_trInd` becomes the trial index and
  `ft_Pos` restarts at 0).
- Temporal binning: **native imaging frames** (3.1777 Hz → 314.7 ms). The reference code only
  re-bins onto *position* (60 bins of 1 dm) for its tuning-curve figures; a decoder that must
  predict position from neural activity has to stay in the time domain, so the native frame
  grid is used here.
- The paper's own quantifications (d′, coding direction) use raw deconvolved traces restricted
  to `ft_CorrSpc & (ft_move > 0)`.

### Curation Steps

**Session/mouse curation rules**: none — all 89 recordings from all 19 mice are analysed in the
paper (different figures use different subsets, but the union is all 89).

**Neuron curation rules**:
- Suite2p ROI detection + cell classification + neuropil correction + deconvolution (upstream).
- Keep neurons assigned to a visual area: `iarea ∉ {−1, 7}` (`Get_density_map`, utils.py:409).
- No activity-based threshold is used in the reference.

**Trial curation rules**:
- No trial-level exclusions in the main analyses. Individual figures apply extra criteria
  (e.g. Fig. 4j uses only rewarded trials with a first lick after 2 m), but these are
  figure-specific and not part of the general pipeline.
- Timepoint-level exclusion: outside 0–4 m, or VR not moving (mouse not running).

### Decoders Trained
| Decoded variable | Accuracy |
|---|---|
| — | The paper reports **no** decoding analyses (grep for "decod", "accura", "classif" in the full text returns nothing). There is therefore no published accuracy to compare against; chance level and internal consistency are used instead. |

---

## Step 4: Check for Consistency
**Status**: COMPLETE

### Discrepancies Found
| Topic | Code says | Data shows | Paper says | Resolution |
|-------|-----------|------------|------------|------------|
| # recordings / mice | 142 db entries in `Imaging_Exp_info` | 89 unique `(mname,datexp,blk)`, 89 spk files, 19 mice | "89 recordings in 19 mice" | The 142 entries are *(recording × experiment-type)* pairs. De-duplicate to 89 recordings. Verified: set of spk filenames == set of recording keys, no extras on either side. |
| # neurons / recording | — | min 20,547, max 89,577 | "20,547 to 89,577 neurons in each recording" | **Exact match** → confirms `load_spk` concatenation order and that `len(iarea)` == n_neurons. |
| Behaviour vs neural length | `nfr = spk.shape[1]`, `beh[...][:nfr]` | `len(ft) = n_frames + 1` | — | Truncate behaviour to `nfr = spk.shape[1]` exactly as the reference does. |
| "Running" definition | `VRmove = ft_move > 0` | `ft_move = diff(ft_PosCum)`; retaining it gives 20–31 frames/trial (median 22 ≈ 4 m ÷ 0.6 m s⁻¹ × 3.18 Hz = 21.2) | "running faster than 6 cm s⁻¹ for ≥66 ms — a threshold that triggers the motion of the virtual reality" | `ft_move > 0` **is** the paper's running criterion (VR motion is triggered by exactly that threshold). Use it. |
| "Corridor" extent | `ft_CorrSpc` | `ft_CorrSpc == (ft_Pos < 40)` exactly (checked, 100 %) | "0–4 m region of the corridors where the textures were shown" | Corridor = 0–4 m = `ft_Pos ∈ [0,40)` dm. The 2 m grey space is excluded, which is also what the decoder's "4 equal 1-m position bins" requires. |
| `isRew` semantics | docstring: "boolean value indicating if the trial is a reward trial"; `get_cat_id` uses `WallName[isRew][0]` to find the rewarded stimulus | For *passive*-reward mice `isRew == (WallName == rewStim)`; for *active-after-cue* mice (TX108, TX109) `isRew.sum() == (~isnan(RewTime)).sum()` and 34 / 11 rewarded-corridor trials have `isRew == False` | "The reward was delivered if a lick was detected after the sound cue in the rewarded corridor" | `isRew` = **reward actually delivered**, not "rewarded corridor". Using it as a decoder *input* would leak the licking *output*. Reward availability is therefore computed as `WallName == rewStim`, where `rewStim = WallName[isRew][0]` exactly as `get_cat_id` does (and 0 for every trial of the unsupervised/naive mice, which never received water). |
| `RunFr` vs `ft_RunSpeed` | notebook: "`RunFr`: same as `ft_RunSpeed`" | `RunFr = 0.3226 × ft_RunSpeed` (r = 0.9997) | running speeds of 6–60 cm s⁻¹ | `ft_RunSpeed` is the one in cm s⁻¹ (range −12 … +69 cm s⁻¹, threshold 6, VR speed 60). Use `ft_RunSpeed`. |
| Canonical stimulus ids | `Get_coding_direction` docstring: `0 circle1, 1 circle2, 2 leaf1, 3 leaf2, 4 leaf3, 5 leaf1_swap1, 6 leaf1_swap2`; `get_cat_id` shows these are **roles** (id 2 = trained/rewarded stimulus) | merging `stim_id` over all experiment types covers 37,801 / 38,110 trials; the only uncovered stimulus is `circle3` (390 trials, 309 of them in 4 sessions with no id) | "we denote the stimuli as 'leaf' and 'circle' even though ... 'rock' and 'bricks' were also used" — i.e. stimuli are pooled by *role* across mice | Use the reference's canonical role ids 0–6 (obtained by merging `stim_id` across every experiment type that contains the recording) and add **id 7 = `circle3`** for the 309 otherwise-unlabelled trials, so no data are dropped. |
| Grey-space frames | `get_interpPos_spk` uses all 60 position bins (6 m) | — | d′/selectivity uses 0–4 m only | Decoder spec asks for "position in corridor discretized into 4 equal-length 1-m bins", i.e. the 4 m texture corridor. Consistent with the d′ recipe; the grey space is excluded. |

All discrepancies resolved; no remaining inconsistency between paper, code and data.

---

## Step 5: Mapping Planning
**Status**: COMPLETE

### Session definition
One converted session = one of the **89 recordings**. Behaviour for a recording is taken from
the *first* experiment type that contains it (they are identical); `stim_id` is merged over
**all** experiment types containing it.

### Timepoint selection (per recording)
```
nfr   = spk.shape[1]                        # reference: load_spk / Get_dprime_selective_neuron
keep  = (ft_move[:nfr] > 0) & ft_CorrSpc[:nfr] & ~isnan(ft_trInd[:nfr])
```
Trial t = the retained frames with `ft_trInd == t`, in time order. Median 22 frames/trial.

### Variable Mapping
| Source Variable | Target Field | Transform | Reference Code Function(s) | Notes |
|-----------------|--------------|-----------|----------------------------|-------|
| `spks` (list of 3 plane arrays) | `neural` | concat along neurons → keep visual-area neurons → keep retained frames → z-score per neuron → subsample 2000 neurons → split by trial | `load_spk`, `Get_dprime_selective_neuron` (`fr_valid`) | float32, (n_neurons, T_trial) |
| `iarea` (retinotopy) | `brain_region_idx` | `neu_area_ID` mapping to `['V1','mHV','lHV','aHV']`; drop `iarea ∈ {−1,7}` | `neu_area_ID`, `Get_density_map` | |
| `SoundTime`, `ft` | `input[0]` "time_to_sound_cue_s" | `(SoundTime[trial] − ft[t]) × 86400`, clipped to ±30 s | `beh['SoundTime']` | continuous, time-varying; >0 before the cue |
| `datexp` | `input[1]` "day_of_training" | days since that mouse's **first** recording | `Imaging_Exp_info` | continuous, per-trial (broadcast over time) |
| `Trial_start_time`, `ft` | `input[2]` "time_since_trial_start_s" | `(ft[t] − Trial_start_time[trial]) × 86400`, clipped to 30 s | `beh['Trial_start_time']` | continuous, time-varying |
| `WallName`, `isRew` | `input[3]` "reward_available" | `1` if `WallName[trial] == WallName[isRew][0]`, else `0`; all-0 for sessions with no rewards | `get_cat_id` | discrete, per-trial |
| `WallName` + merged `stim_id` | `output[0]` "stimulus" | canonical role id 0–6, plus 7 for `circle3` | `Get_coding_direction` docstring, `get_cat_id` | per-trial (broadcast) |
| `LickFr` | `output[1]` "licking" | `1` for frames `floor(LickFr)`, else 0 | `spk_2_firstLick` (`beh['LickFr'].astype(int)`) | binary, time-varying |
| `ft_Pos` | `output[2]` "position_bin" | `floor(ft_Pos/10)` clipped to 0–3 → 4 bins of 1 m over 0–4 m | corridor geometry (`Texture_Length=40` dm) | time-varying |
| `ft_RunSpeed` | `output[3]` "running_speed_bin" | quartile bin (0–3) using **global** quartiles over all retained timepoints | Methods "Running speed" | time-varying |
| `mname` | `subjects` / `subject_idx` | 19 unique | | |

### Key Decisions
1. **All 89 recordings / 19 mice are kept.** The paper analyses all of them; no session-level
   quality criterion exists in code or text.
2. **Timepoints: `(ft_move>0) & ft_CorrSpc`.** Identical to `fr_valid` in
   `Get_dprime_selective_neuron` and to the Methods ("0–4 m region", "excluded the data points
   in which the animal was not running"). It also removes the reward-collection stops, exactly
   as the paper intends.
3. **Native imaging frames as time bins** (314.7 ms; frame rate varies by <0.4 % across
   sessions, so a single `time_bin_size` is reported). No re-binning — the imaging rate is
   already slow, and the paper's only re-binning is onto position, which cannot be used when
   position is a decoder target.
4. **Neurons: visual-cortex only (`iarea ∉ {−1,7}`), then a seeded random subsample of up to
   2000 per session, stratified proportionally over V1/mHV/lHV/aHV.**
   Rationale: 4.1 M visual neurons × 821 k timepoints is ~150 GB and would make both the pickle
   and the 200-epoch decoder training intractable (every epoch copies the whole dataset to the
   GPU). 2000 is exactly `decoder.train_decoder`'s `svd_max_neurons` default, so the SVD
   initialisation is computed on the true neurons rather than on a random Gaussian projection.
   Stratifying keeps each session's area composition. Seeded → reproducible.
5. **Neural activity is z-scored per neuron** over the retained timepoints of its session.
   Deconvolved Suite2p amplitudes are in arbitrary, wildly heterogeneous units (per-neuron s.d.
   spans 0.5 – 350 within one session; values up to 2849). The decoder initialises its
   projection with an **uncentred** SVD and then feeds the projections straight into a linear
   layer at lr = 1e-3, so raw amplitudes produce saturated logits. Z-scoring makes the SVD a
   true PCA and is the standard preprocessing for deconvolved traces in this lab's pipelines.
   This is the one deliberate deviation from the reference, required by "training a neural
   decoder"; it is a per-neuron affine rescaling and therefore changes no relative structure.
6. **Reward availability = rewarded *corridor*, not reward delivered** (see Step 4). Prevents
   leaking the licking output into the decoder input.
7. **Stimulus = canonical role id** (0 circle1, 1 circle2, 2 leaf1, 3 leaf2, 4 leaf3,
   5 leaf1_swap1, 6 leaf1_swap2, 7 circle3). Pools rock/brick mice onto the leaf/circle roles
   exactly as the paper does, giving one label set that means the same thing in every session.
8. **Time inputs clipped to ±30 s.** Wall-clock time is used (not "running time"), because that
   is the true time since corridor entry and because running-frame counts would make position
   a deterministic function of the input. ~2 % of retained samples come from trials in which the
   mouse paused for tens of seconds inside the corridor (max 400 s); clipping keeps the linear
   decoder well conditioned without discarding any data.
9. **Running-speed bins from global quartiles** — the spec says each bin should hold 25 % of
   the data, which is only exactly true if the quantiles are computed over the pooled dataset.
10. **No trials are dropped.** Every one of the 38,110 trials has ≥1 retained frame (verified).

### Planned Sanity Checks
- [ ] 89 sessions, 19 mice, 38,110 trials, 821,579 timepoints in the converted file.
- [ ] Per-session total neurons (before area filtering) min 20,547 / max 89,577 (paper).
- [ ] `len(iarea) == spk.shape[0]` for every session.
- [ ] Median frames per trial ≈ 21–22 (= 4 m / 0.6 m s⁻¹ × 3.18 Hz).
- [ ] Position bin 0→3 increases monotonically within a trial; first frame in bin 0.
- [ ] Reconstructed position from `output[2]` matches raw `ft_Pos` bins (independent reload).
- [ ] Lick fraction per session ~5–20 %; task mice lick more in the rewarded corridor.
- [ ] Running-speed bins each hold 25.0 % of timepoints globally.
- [ ] Reward-available trials = 4,446 (11.7 %), all in the 28 task sessions from 5 mice.
- [ ] Stimulus id distribution matches the counts computed from raw `WallName` + `stim_id`.
- [ ] Spot-check `neural[s][t][n, k]` against a fresh `np.load` of the spk file.
- [ ] `time_to_sound_cue` crosses 0 at the frame nearest `SoundFr`.

### Processing Details
+- Temporal alignment for the decoder task: **trial start = corridor entry**
+  (`Trial_start_time`, i.e. the frame at which `ft_trInd` becomes the trial index and
+  `ft_Pos` restarts at 0).
+- Temporal binning: **native imaging frames** (3.1777 Hz → 314.7 ms). The reference code only
+  re-bins onto *position* (60 bins of 1 dm) for its tuning-curve figures; a decoder that must
+  predict position from neural activity has to stay in the time domain, so the native frame
+  grid is used here.
+- The paper's own quantifications (d′, coding direction) use raw deconvolved traces restricted
+  to `ft_CorrSpc & (ft_move > 0)`.
### Curation Steps
+**Session/mouse curation rules**: none — all 89 recordings from all 19 mice are analysed in the
+paper (different figures use different subsets, but the union is all 89).
**Neuron curation rules**:
+- Suite2p ROI detection + cell classification + neuropil correction + deconvolution (upstream).
+- Keep neurons assigned to a visual area: `iarea ∉ {−1, 7}` (`Get_density_map`, utils.py:409).
+- No activity-based threshold is used in the reference.
**Trial curation rules**:
+- No trial-level exclusions in the main analyses. Individual figures apply extra criteria
+  (e.g. Fig. 4j uses only rewarded trials with a first lick after 2 m), but these are
+  figure-specific and not part of the general pipeline.
+- Timepoint-level exclusion: outside 0–4 m, or VR not moving (mouse not running).
### Decoders Trained
| Decoded variable | Accuracy |

+| — | The paper reports **no** decoding analyses (grep for "decod", "accura", "classif" in the full text returns nothing). There is therefore no published accuracy to compare against; chance level and internal consistency are used instead. |

+| `WallName` + merged `stim_id` | `output[0]` "stimulus" | canonical role id 0–6, plus 7 for `circle3` | `Get_coding_direction` docstring, `get_cat_id` | per-trial (broadcast) |
+| `LickFr` | `output[1]` "licking" | `1` for frames `floor(LickFr)`, else 0 | `spk_2_firstLick` (`beh['LickFr'].astype(int)`) | binary, time-varying |
+| `ft_Pos` | `output[2]` "position_bin" | `floor(ft_Pos/10)` clipped to 0–3 → 4 bins of 1 m over 0–4 m | corridor geometry (`Texture_Length=40` dm) | time-varying |
+| `ft_RunSpeed` | `output[3]` "running_speed_bin" | quartile bin (0–3) using **global** quartiles over all retained timepoints | Methods "Running speed" | time-varying |
+| `mname` | `subjects` / `subject_idx` | 19 unique | | |
### Key Decisions
+1. **All 89 recordings / 19 mice are kept.** The paper analyses all of them; no session-level
+   quality criterion exists in code or text.
+2. **Timepoints: `(ft_move>0) & ft_CorrSpc`.** Identical to `fr_valid` in
+   `Get_dprime_selective_neuron` and to the Methods ("0–4 m region", "excluded the data points
+   in which the animal was not running"). It also removes the reward-collection stops, exactly
+   as the paper intends.
+3. **Native imaging frames as time bins** (314.7 ms; frame rate varies by <0.4 % across
+   sessions, so a single `time_bin_size` is reported). No re-binning — the imaging rate is
+   already slow, and the paper's only re-binning is onto position, which cannot be used when
+   position is a decoder target.
+4. **Neurons: visual-cortex only (`iarea ∉ {−1,7}`), then a seeded random subsample of up to
+   2000 per session, stratified proportionally over V1/mHV/lHV/aHV.**
+   Rationale: 4.1 M visual neurons × 821 k timepoints is ~150 GB and would make both the pickle
+   and the 200-epoch decoder training intractable (every epoch copies the whole dataset to the
+   GPU). 2000 is exactly `decoder.train_decoder`'s `svd_max_neurons` default, so the SVD
+   initialisation is computed on the true neurons rather than on a random Gaussian projection.
+   Stratifying keeps each session's area composition. Seeded → reproducible.
+5. **Neural activity is z-scored per neuron** over the retained timepoints of its session.
+   Deconvolved Suite2p amplitudes are in arbitrary, wildly heterogeneous units (per-neuron s.d.
+   spans 0.5 – 350 within one session; values up to 2849). The decoder initialises its
+   projection with an **uncentred** SVD and then feeds the projections straight into a linear
+   layer at lr = 1e-3, so raw amplitudes produce saturated logits. Z-scoring makes the SVD a
+   true PCA and is the standard preprocessing for deconvolved traces in this lab's pipelines.
+   This is the one deliberate deviation from the reference, required by "training a neural
+   decoder"; it is a per-neuron affine rescaling and therefore changes no relative structure.
+6. **Reward availability = rewarded *corridor*, not reward delivered** (see Step 4). Prevents
+   leaking the licking output into the decoder input.
+7. **Stimulus = canonical role id** (0 circle1, 1 circle2, 2 leaf1, 3 leaf2, 4 leaf3,
+   5 leaf1_swap1, 6 leaf1_swap2, 7 circle3). Pools rock/brick mice onto the leaf/circle roles
+   exactly as the paper does, giving one label set that means the same thing in every session.
+8. **Time inputs clipped to ±30 s.** Wall-clock time is used (not "running time"), because that
+   is the true time since corridor entry and because running-frame counts would make position
+   a deterministic function of the input. ~2 % of retained samples come from trials in which the
+   mouse paused for tens of seconds inside the corridor (max 400 s); clipping keeps the linear
+   decoder well conditioned without discarding any data.
+9. **Running-speed bins from global quartiles** — the spec says each bin should hold 25 % of
+   the data, which is only exactly true if the quantiles are computed over the pooled dataset.
+10. **No trials are dropped.** Every one of the 38,110 trials has ≥1 retained frame (verified).
### Planned Sanity Checks
+- [ ] 89 sessions, 19 mice, 38,110 trials, 821,579 timepoints in the converted file.
+- [ ] Per-session total neurons (before area filtering) min 20,547 / max 89,577 (paper).
+- [ ] `len(iarea) == spk.shape[0]` for every session.
+- [ ] Median frames per trial ≈ 21–22 (= 4 m / 0.6 m s⁻¹ × 3.18 Hz).
+- [ ] Position bin 0→3 increases monotonically within a trial; first frame in bin 0.
+- [ ] Reconstructed position from `output[2]` matches raw `ft_Pos` bins (independent reload).
+- [ ] Lick fraction per session ~5–20 %; task mice lick more in the rewarded corridor.
+- [ ] Running-speed bins each hold 25.0 % of timepoints globally.
+- [ ] Reward-available trials = 4,446 (11.7 %), all in the 28 task sessions from 5 mice.
+- [ ] Stimulus id distribution matches the counts computed from raw `WallName` + `stim_id`.
+- [ ] Spot-check `neural[s][t][n, k]` against a fresh `np.load` of the spk file.
+- [ ] `time_to_sound_cue` crosses 0 at the frame nearest `SoundFr`.

# Dataset Conversion Notes

## Overview
- **Dataset**: Zhong, Baptista, Gattoni, Arnold, Flickinger, Stringer & Pachitariu,
  *"Unsupervised pretraining in biological neural networks"* (`/app/paper.pdf`).
  Two-photon mesoscope calcium imaging of mouse visual cortex during a virtual-reality
  visual-discrimination task. Figshare DOI 10.25378/janelia.28811129.v1
- **Date started**: 2026-09-19
- **Goal**: Convert to decoder-compatible format (`/app/converted_data.pkl`)

---

## Step 0: Setup and Initialization
**Status**: COMPLETE

Environment verified: `numpy 2.4.4`, `torch 2.6.0+cu124`, `scipy 1.18.0`, `h5py 3.16.0`.
Hardware: 1006 GB RAM, 128 CPUs, 1x NVIDIA L4 (23 GB).

Directory contents of `/app`:
- `.manifest`, `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yaml`
- `CONVERSION_NOTES.md` (this file)
- `paper.pdf` (25 pages), `methods.txt` (excerpt of paper methods)
- `decoder.py` (89 KB, decoder library), `train_decoder.py` (validation/training driver)
- `code/` — reference code from the paper:
  `README.md`, `LICENSE`, `utils.py` (947 lines), `data_process_script.ipynb`,
  `Figures.ipynb`, `fig1.py`, `fig2.py`, `fig3.py`, `fig4.py`, `fig5.py`, `S6.py`
- `data/`
  - `data/beh/` (6.6 GB): 23 `Beh_<exp_type>.npy` files, `Imaging_Exp_info.npy`,
    `example_bef_and_aft_learning_behavior.npy`, `Unsupervised_pretraining_behavior/` (3 files)
  - `data/spk/` (405 GB): 89 `<mouse>_<date>_<blk>_neural_data.npy` files
  - `data/retinotopy/` (170 MB): 89 `<mouse>_<date>_trans.npz` + `areas.npz`
  - `data/process_data/` (empty — intermediate results are regenerated by the reference notebook)

---

## Step 1: Reference Code Exploration
**Status**: COMPLETE

### Key Functions Identified

| Function | File | Stage | Purpose |
|----------|------|-------|---------|
| `download_data_from_figshare` | utils.py:12 | LOADING | Downloads `spk/`, `beh/`, `retinotopy/` from Figshare; defines the directory layout |
| `load_exp_beh(root, exp_type)` | utils.py:326 | LOADING | `np.load('beh/Beh_<exp_type>.npy').item()` → dict keyed by `<mname>_<datexp>_<blk>[_<stimtype>]` |
| `load_spk(db, root)` | utils.py:338 | LOADING | `np.concatenate(np.load('<mname>_<datexp>_<blk>_neural_data.npy').item()['spks'], 0)` → (n_neurons, n_frames) deconvolved traces |
| `load_retino(db, root)` | utils.py:330 | LOADING | Loads `<mname>_<datexp>_trans.npz`; returns `xy_t`, `iarea`, and `neu_ar_idx` (per-area boolean masks) |
| `neu_area_ID(iarea)` | utils.py:312 | CURATION | Maps `iarea` code → visual area: **V1** = 8; **mHV** = 0,1,2,9; **lHV** = 5,6; **aHV** = 3,4. Codes −1 and 7 are *not* in any area |
| `Get_dprime_selective_neuron` | utils.py:418 | PROCESSING | Canonical frame-selection recipe: `fr_valid = (ft_move[:nfr] > 0) & ft_CorrSpc[:nfr]` — "only use activity inside the texture area plus mouse is running (VR moving)" |
| `Get_density_map` | utils.py:394 | CURATION | `idx_neu = (iarea != -1) & (iarea != 7)` — "exclude neurons from outside of visual cortex" |
| `dprime(x1, x2)` | utils.py:370 | PROCESSING | `2*(µ1−µ2)/(σ1+σ2)` on raw deconvolved traces |
| `spk_pos_interp` / `get_interpPos_spk` | utils.py:105/120 | PROCESSING | Interpolates activity onto 60 position bins per trial (1 dm each, 6 m of VR). Used for the paper's position-tuning figures only |
| `get_cat_id(WallName, isRew)` | utils.py:137 | PROCESSING | Assigns canonical stimulus roles from the *rewarded* wall: rewarded stim → 2, its "2" variant → 3, other stim → 0, its "2" variant → 1 |
| `get_lick_raster`, `lick_response` | utils.py:149/238 | PROCESSING | Behavioural lick analyses; use `LickPos`/`LickTrind` |
| `spk_2_firstLick`, `spk_2_cue` | utils.py:913/935 | PROCESSING | Event-aligned activity; **uses `beh['LickFr'].astype(int)` and `beh['SoundFr'].astype(int)`** — i.e. event frame indices are *truncated* (floor) to the containing imaging frame |
| `data_process_script.ipynb` cell 9 | code/ | PROCESSING | Top-level loop: `VRmove = beh['ft_move'][:nfr] > 0`, `ft_AcumPos = beh['ft_PosCum'][:nfr]`, then position interpolation with `n_bins=60, lengths=Corridor_Length` |

### Notes
- Neural data are **deconvolved** Suite2p traces (`spks`), stored as a list of 3 sub-arrays
  (imaging planes/slices) that are concatenated along the neuron axis. No ΔF/F needs to be
  computed — the paper states "All our analyses were based on deconvolved fluorescence traces".
- No spike-sorting quality filtering exists (this is imaging, not ephys). Suite2p's own cell
  classifier has already been applied upstream. The only neuron curation in the reference code
  is **anatomical**: keep neurons assigned to a visual area (`iarea ∉ {−1, 7}`).
- The reference code **truncates behaviour to the number of neural frames**: `nfr = spk.shape[1]`,
  then `beh['ft_*'][:nfr]`. The behaviour arrays are 1 frame longer than the imaging arrays.
- The reference never normalises `spks` before analysis (it uses d′, which is scale-free).
- `data_process_script.ipynb` documents every `beh` field (copied into Step 2 below).

---

## Step 2: Dataset Exploration
**Status**: COMPLETE

### Data Structure

**`data/beh/Imaging_Exp_info.npy`** → dict with 23 *experiment types* (keys):
`unsup_train1_before_learning`, `unsup_train1_after_learning`, `sup_train1_before_learning`,
`sup_train1_after_learning`, `unsup_test1`, `sup_test1`, `naive_test1`, `unsup_test2`,
`sup_test2`, `naive_test2`, `unsup_test3`, `sup_test3`, `naive_test3`,
`unsup_train2_before_learning`, `sup_train2_before_learning`, `unsup_train2_after_learning`,
`sup_train2_after_learning`, `train1_before_grating`, `train1_after_grating`,
`test1_before_grating`, `test1_after_grating`, `test2_before_grating`, `test2_after_grating`.

Each value is a list of "db" dicts: `mname`, `datexp`, `blk`, optional `stimtype`
(`swap1`/`swap2`), `exptype` (`sup`/`unsup`/`naive`/absent), `rewType`, `stim_id`
(canonical id for each entry of `UniqWalls`, `NaN` where not used in that comparison), etc.
**142 db entries → 89 unique recordings** (a recording can appear under several experiment
types, e.g. a `test1` session is also the `train2_before_learning` session).

**`data/beh/Beh_<exp_type>.npy`** → dict keyed `<mname>_<datexp>_<blk>[_<stimtype>]`. All entries
for the same recording carry identical behaviour (same `ntrials`, same `ft`); they differ only
in the `stim_id` labelling supplied by `Imaging_Exp_info`.

Behaviour fields used here (definitions from `data_process_script.ipynb`):

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ntrials` | number of corridor traversals |
| `Corridor_Length` = 60, `Texture_Length` = 40, `Gray_Space_length` = 20 | in **decimetres**: 4 m of texture + 2 m of grey |
| `ft` (n_frames,) | MATLAB datenum timestamp of each **imaging frame** |
| `ft_trInd` | trial index of each frame (NaN outside behaviour) |
| `ft_Pos`, `ft_PosCum` | position in VR (dm) per frame; cumulative |
| `ft_move` | `diff(ft_PosCum)` — >0 iff the VR advanced during that frame |
| `ft_CorrSpc`, `ft_GraySpc` | in texture area (`ft_Pos < 40`) / in grey (`ft_Pos ≥ 40`) — verified exactly |
| `ft_RunSpeed` (= `RunFr` up to a constant scale) | ball running speed interpolated to imaging frames (cm s⁻¹) |
| `ft_WallID` | stimulus name of the corridor each frame belongs to |
| `Trial_start_time`, `Trial_end_time`, `Gray_space_time` | wall-clock times of corridor entry / exit / grey entry |
| `StartFr`, `GrayFr`, `EndFr`, `SoundFr`, `SoundDelayFr`, `RewardFr`, `LickFr` | (fractional) imaging-frame indices of the same events |
| `SoundTime`, `SoundTimeDelay`, `SoundPos` | time / position of the sound cue (per trial) |
| `RewTime`, `RewPos`, `isRew` | reward delivery time/position; `isRew` = reward **was delivered** |
| `WallName`, `UniqWalls`, `stim_id` | stimulus per trial / unique stimuli / canonical ids |
| `LickTime`, `LickPos`, `LickTrind`, `LickFr` | one entry per lick |

**`data/spk/<mname>_<datexp>_<blk>_neural_data.npy`** → `{'spks': [3 float32 arrays]}`, each
`(n_neurons_plane, n_frames)`; concatenated along axis 0 gives `(n_neurons, n_frames)`
deconvolved activity. `n_frames` = `len(ft) − 1` in the sessions checked.

**`data/retinotopy/<mname>_<datexp>_trans.npz`** → `xy_t` (n_neurons, 2) cortical coordinates,
`iarea` (n_neurons,) area code, `xpos`, `ypos`, `A`. `len(iarea)` equals the concatenated
neuron count of the matching `spk` file (verified). `areas.npz` holds the 10 area outlines.

### Dataset Size (from data files)
| Statistic | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Subjects (mice) | **19** (`DR10, DR15, LZ13, LZ16, TX104, TX105, TX108, TX109, TX119, TX123, TX124, TX139, TX140, TX60, TX61, TX83, TX85, TX88, VR2`) |
| Sessions (recordings) | **89** (89 spk files ↔ 89 unique `Imaging_Exp_info` recordings, exact match) |
| Sessions / subject | 1–8 (mean 4.7) |
| Neurons (total, all recorded) | 4,691,034 (mean 52,708 / session; **min 20,547, max 89,577**) |
| Neurons in a visual area (`iarea ∉ {−1,7}`) | 4,105,393 (mean 46,128; min 17,363, max 78,815) |
| Trials (total) | **38,110** (mean 428 / session; range 84–789) |
| Imaging frame rate | 3.171–3.181 Hz across sessions (median **3.1777 Hz** → 314.7 ms bin) |
| Timepoints in corridor while VR moving | **821,579** (mean 9,231 / session; median 22 frames / trial) |
| Trials in a rewarded corridor | 4,446 / 38,110 = 11.7 % (28 sessions from 5 task mice) |

Stimulus (`WallName`) counts over all 38,110 trials:
`leaf1 9736, circle1 9393, leaf2 4841, rock1 2743, wood1 2517, circle2 1836, wood2 1592,
leaf3 1545, leaf1_swap2 821, leaf1_swap1 818, wood5 567, rock2 535, wood1_swap2 421,
circle3 390, wood1_swap1 355`.

---

## Step 3: Reference Text Reading
**Status**: COMPLETE

### Expected Statistics (from paper/methods)
| Statistic | Value | Source Quote |
|-----------|-------|--------------|
| Recordings | 89 | "We performed 89 recordings in 19 mice" |
| Subjects | 19 | same |
| Neurons / recording | 20,547 – 89,577 | "activity traces from 20,547 to 89,577 neurons in each recording" |
| Corridor geometry | 4 m corridor + 2 m grey | "The virtual reality corridors were each 4 m long, with 2 m of grey space between corridors" |
| VR speed | 60 cm s⁻¹ (constant while running) | "the virtual corridors always moved at a constant speed (60 cm s−1)" |
| Running threshold | 6 cm s⁻¹ for ≥66 ms | "running faster than a threshold of 6 cm s−1"; "faster than 6 cm s−1 for at least 66 ms (a threshold that triggers the motion of the virtual reality)" |
| Sound-cue position | uniform 0.5 – 3.5 m | "the time of the sound cue was randomly chosen per trial from a uniform distribution between positions 0.5 m and 3.5 m" (data: 0.4 – 3.9 m) |
| Neural signal | deconvolved Suite2p traces, τ_decay = 0.75 s | "For non-negative deconvolution, we used a timescale of decay of 0.75 s. All our analyses were based on deconvolved fluorescence traces" |
| Calcium frame rate | 3.17 Hz | `data_process_script.ipynb`: "Calcium signal recording frame rate: fs = 3.17Hz" |
| Analysis window | 0–4 m of the corridor | "we only selected data points inside the 0–4-m region of the corridors where the textures were shown" |
| Data exclusion | non-running timepoints removed | "We excluded the data points in which the animal was not running, so that all data points included ... came from similar engagement or arousal levels"; "We only considered timepoints during running for analysis, which removed time periods when the task mice stopped to collect water rewards" |
| Selective-neuron criterion (paper analyses only) | d′ ≥ 0.3 | "The criteria for selective neurons was d′ ≥ 0.3" |
| Brain regions | V1, medial HV, lateral HV, anterior HV | Figs. 1j, 2i, 3 use `['V1','mHV','lHV','aHV']` |
| Cohorts | 5 task (sup) mice, 7–9 unsupervised, 9 naive (11 sessions), VRg gratings mice | Fig. 3/Ext. Data Fig. 3 legends |
| Reward rate | rewarded corridor is 1 of the 2 trained corridors (≈50 % of trials in task sessions) | "For task mice, the sound cue indicated the beginning of the reward zone in the rewarded corridor" |
| Stimulus naming | leaf/circle (also rock/brick in some mice) | "we denote the stimuli as 'leaf' and 'circle', even though other visual stimuli were also used in some mice ('rock' and 'bricks')" |

### Processing Details
- Temporal alignment for the decoder task: **trial start = corridor entry**
  (`Trial_start_time`, i.e. the frame at which `ft_trInd` becomes the trial index and
  `ft_Pos` restarts at 0).
- Temporal binning: **native imaging frames** (3.1777 Hz → 314.7 ms). The reference code only
  re-bins onto *position* (60 bins of 1 dm) for its tuning-curve figures; a decoder that must
  predict position from neural activity has to stay in the time domain, so the native frame
  grid is used here.
- The paper's own quantifications (d′, coding direction) use raw deconvolved traces restricted
  to `ft_CorrSpc & (ft_move > 0)`.

### Curation Steps

**Session/mouse curation rules**: none — all 89 recordings from all 19 mice are analysed in the
paper (different figures use different subsets, but the union is all 89).

**Neuron curation rules**:
- Suite2p ROI detection + cell classification + neuropil correction + deconvolution (upstream).
- Keep neurons assigned to a visual area: `iarea ∉ {−1, 7}` (`Get_density_map`, utils.py:409).
- No activity-based threshold is used in the reference.

**Trial curation rules**:
- No trial-level exclusions in the main analyses. Individual figures apply extra criteria
  (e.g. Fig. 4j uses only rewarded trials with a first lick after 2 m), but these are
  figure-specific and not part of the general pipeline.
- Timepoint-level exclusion: outside 0–4 m, or VR not moving (mouse not running).

### Decoders Trained
| Decoded variable | Accuracy |
|---|---|
| — | The paper reports **no** decoding analyses (grep for "decod", "accura", "classif" in the full text returns nothing). There is therefore no published accuracy to compare against; chance level and internal consistency are used instead. |

---

## Step 4: Check for Consistency
**Status**: COMPLETE

### Discrepancies Found
| Topic | Code says | Data shows | Paper says | Resolution |
|-------|-----------|------------|------------|------------|
| # recordings / mice | 142 db entries in `Imaging_Exp_info` | 89 unique `(mname,datexp,blk)`, 89 spk files, 19 mice | "89 recordings in 19 mice" | The 142 entries are *(recording × experiment-type)* pairs. De-duplicate to 89 recordings. Verified: set of spk filenames == set of recording keys, no extras on either side. |
| # neurons / recording | — | min 20,547, max 89,577 | "20,547 to 89,577 neurons in each recording" | **Exact match** → confirms `load_spk` concatenation order and that `len(iarea)` == n_neurons. |
| Behaviour vs neural length | `nfr = spk.shape[1]`, `beh[...][:nfr]` | `len(ft) = n_frames + 1` | — | Truncate behaviour to `nfr = spk.shape[1]` exactly as the reference does. |
| "Running" definition | `VRmove = ft_move > 0` | `ft_move = diff(ft_PosCum)`; retaining it gives 20–31 frames/trial (median 22 ≈ 4 m ÷ 0.6 m s⁻¹ × 3.18 Hz = 21.2) | "running faster than 6 cm s⁻¹ for ≥66 ms — a threshold that triggers the motion of the virtual reality" | `ft_move > 0` **is** the paper's running criterion (VR motion is triggered by exactly that threshold). Use it. |
| "Corridor" extent | `ft_CorrSpc` | `ft_CorrSpc == (ft_Pos < 40)` exactly (checked, 100 %) | "0–4 m region of the corridors where the textures were shown" | Corridor = 0–4 m = `ft_Pos ∈ [0,40)` dm. The 2 m grey space is excluded, which is also what the decoder's "4 equal 1-m position bins" requires. |
| `isRew` semantics | docstring: "boolean value indicating if the trial is a reward trial"; `get_cat_id` uses `WallName[isRew][0]` to find the rewarded stimulus | For *passive*-reward mice `isRew == (WallName == rewStim)`; for *active-after-cue* mice (TX108, TX109) `isRew.sum() == (~isnan(RewTime)).sum()` and 34 / 11 rewarded-corridor trials have `isRew == False` | "The reward was delivered if a lick was detected after the sound cue in the rewarded corridor" | `isRew` = **reward actually delivered**, not "rewarded corridor". Using it as a decoder *input* would leak the licking *output*. Reward availability is therefore computed as `WallName == rewStim`, where `rewStim = WallName[isRew][0]` exactly as `get_cat_id` does (and 0 for every trial of the unsupervised/naive mice, which never received water). |
| `RunFr` vs `ft_RunSpeed` | notebook: "`RunFr`: same as `ft_RunSpeed`" | `RunFr = 0.3226 × ft_RunSpeed` (r = 0.9997) | running speeds of 6–60 cm s⁻¹ | `ft_RunSpeed` is the one in cm s⁻¹ (range −12 … +69 cm s⁻¹, threshold 6, VR speed 60). Use `ft_RunSpeed`. |
| Canonical stimulus ids | `Get_coding_direction` docstring: `0 circle1, 1 circle2, 2 leaf1, 3 leaf2, 4 leaf3, 5 leaf1_swap1, 6 leaf1_swap2`; `get_cat_id` shows these are **roles** (id 2 = trained/rewarded stimulus) | merging `stim_id` over all experiment types covers 37,801 / 38,110 trials; the only uncovered stimulus is `circle3` (390 trials, 309 of them in 4 sessions with no id) | "we denote the stimuli as 'leaf' and 'circle' even though ... 'rock' and 'bricks' were also used" — i.e. stimuli are pooled by *role* across mice | Use the reference's canonical role ids 0–6 (obtained by merging `stim_id` across every experiment type that contains the recording) and add **id 7 = `circle3`** for the 309 otherwise-unlabelled trials, so no data are dropped. |
| Grey-space frames | `get_interpPos_spk` uses all 60 position bins (6 m) | — | d′/selectivity uses 0–4 m only | Decoder spec asks for "position in corridor discretized into 4 equal-length 1-m bins", i.e. the 4 m texture corridor. Consistent with the d′ recipe; the grey space is excluded. |

All discrepancies resolved; no remaining inconsistency between paper, code and data.

---

## Step 5: Mapping Planning
**Status**: COMPLETE

### Session definition
One converted session = one of the **89 recordings**. Behaviour for a recording is taken from
the *first* experiment type that contains it (they are identical); `stim_id` is merged over
**all** experiment types containing it.

### Timepoint selection (per recording)
```
nfr   = spk.shape[1]                        # reference: load_spk / Get_dprime_selective_neuron
keep  = (ft_move[:nfr] > 0) & ft_CorrSpc[:nfr] & ~isnan(ft_trInd[:nfr])
```
Trial t = the retained frames with `ft_trInd == t`, in time order. Median 22 frames/trial.

### Variable Mapping
| Source Variable | Target Field | Transform | Reference Code Function(s) | Notes |
|-----------------|--------------|-----------|----------------------------|-------|
| `spks` (list of 3 plane arrays) | `neural` | concat along neurons → keep visual-area neurons → keep retained frames → z-score per neuron → subsample 2000 neurons → split by trial | `load_spk`, `Get_dprime_selective_neuron` (`fr_valid`) | float32, (n_neurons, T_trial) |
| `iarea` (retinotopy) | `brain_region_idx` | `neu_area_ID` mapping to `['V1','mHV','lHV','aHV']`; drop `iarea ∈ {−1,7}` | `neu_area_ID`, `Get_density_map` | |
| `SoundTime`, `ft` | `input[0]` "time_to_sound_cue_s" | `(SoundTime[trial] − ft[t]) × 86400`, clipped to ±30 s | `beh['SoundTime']` | continuous, time-varying; >0 before the cue |
| `datexp` | `input[1]` "day_of_training" | days since that mouse's **first** recording | `Imaging_Exp_info` | continuous, per-trial (broadcast over time) |
| `Trial_start_time`, `ft` | `input[2]` "time_since_trial_start_s" | `(ft[t] − Trial_start_time[trial]) × 86400`, clipped to 30 s | `beh['Trial_start_time']` | continuous, time-varying |
| `WallName`, `isRew` | `input[3]` "reward_available" | `1` if `WallName[trial] == WallName[isRew][0]`, else `0`; all-0 for sessions with no rewards | `get_cat_id` | discrete, per-trial |
| `WallName` + merged `stim_id` | `output[0]` "stimulus" | canonical role id 0–6, plus 7 for `circle3` | `Get_coding_direction` docstring, `get_cat_id` | per-trial (broadcast) |
| `LickFr` | `output[1]` "licking" | `1` for frames `floor(LickFr)`, else 0 | `spk_2_firstLick` (`beh['LickFr'].astype(int)`) | binary, time-varying |
| `ft_Pos` | `output[2]` "position_bin" | `floor(ft_Pos/10)` clipped to 0–3 → 4 bins of 1 m over 0–4 m | corridor geometry (`Texture_Length=40` dm) | time-varying |
| `ft_RunSpeed` | `output[3]` "running_speed_bin" | quartile bin (0–3) using **global** quartiles over all retained timepoints | Methods "Running speed" | time-varying |
| `mname` | `subjects` / `subject_idx` | 19 unique | | |

### Key Decisions
1. **All 89 recordings / 19 mice are kept.** The paper analyses all of them; no session-level
   quality criterion exists in code or text.
2. **Timepoints: `(ft_move>0) & ft_CorrSpc`.** Identical to `fr_valid` in
   `Get_dprime_selective_neuron` and to the Methods ("0–4 m region", "excluded the data points
   in which the animal was not running"). It also removes the reward-collection stops, exactly
   as the paper intends.
3. **Native imaging frames as time bins** (314.7 ms; frame rate varies by <0.4 % across
   sessions, so a single `time_bin_size` is reported). No re-binning — the imaging rate is
   already slow, and the paper's only re-binning is onto position, which cannot be used when
   position is a decoder target.
4. **Neurons: visual-cortex only (`iarea ∉ {−1,7}`), then a seeded random subsample of up to
   2000 per session, stratified proportionally over V1/mHV/lHV/aHV.**
   Rationale: 4.1 M visual neurons × 821 k timepoints is ~150 GB and would make both the pickle
   and the 200-epoch decoder training intractable (every epoch copies the whole dataset to the
   GPU). 2000 is exactly `decoder.train_decoder`'s `svd_max_neurons` default, so the SVD
   initialisation is computed on the true neurons rather than on a random Gaussian projection.
   Stratifying keeps each session's area composition. Seeded → reproducible.
5. **Neural activity is z-scored per neuron** over the retained timepoints of its session.
   Deconvolved Suite2p amplitudes are in arbitrary, wildly heterogeneous units (per-neuron s.d.
   spans 0.5 – 350 within one session; values up to 2849). The decoder initialises its
   projection with an **uncentred** SVD and then feeds the projections straight into a linear
   layer at lr = 1e-3, so raw amplitudes produce saturated logits. Z-scoring makes the SVD a
   true PCA and is the standard preprocessing for deconvolved traces in this lab's pipelines.
   This is the one deliberate deviation from the reference, required by "training a neural
   decoder"; it is a per-neuron affine rescaling and therefore changes no relative structure.
6. **Reward availability = rewarded *corridor*, not reward delivered** (see Step 4). Prevents
   leaking the licking output into the decoder input.
7. **Stimulus = canonical role id** (0 circle1, 1 circle2, 2 leaf1, 3 leaf2, 4 leaf3,
   5 leaf1_swap1, 6 leaf1_swap2, 7 circle3). Pools rock/brick mice onto the leaf/circle roles
   exactly as the paper does, giving one label set that means the same thing in every session.
8. **Time inputs clipped to ±30 s.** Wall-clock time is used (not "running time"), because that
   is the true time since corridor entry and because running-frame counts would make position
   a deterministic function of the input. ~2 % of retained samples come from trials in which the
   mouse paused for tens of seconds inside the corridor (max 400 s); clipping keeps the linear
   decoder well conditioned without discarding any data.
9. **Running-speed bins from global quartiles** — the spec says each bin should hold 25 % of
   the data, which is only exactly true if the quantiles are computed over the pooled dataset.
10. **No trials are dropped.** Every one of the 38,110 trials has ≥1 retained frame (verified).

### Planned Sanity Checks
- [ ] 89 sessions, 19 mice, 38,110 trials, 821,579 timepoints in the converted file.
- [ ] Per-session total neurons (before area filtering) min 20,547 / max 89,577 (paper).
- [ ] `len(iarea) == spk.shape[0]` for every session.
- [ ] Median frames per trial ≈ 21–22 (= 4 m / 0.6 m s⁻¹ × 3.18 Hz).
- [ ] Position bin 0→3 increases monotonically within a trial; first frame in bin 0.
- [ ] Reconstructed position from `output[2]` matches raw `ft_Pos` bins (independent reload).
- [ ] Lick fraction per session ~5–20 %; task mice lick more in the rewarded corridor.
- [ ] Running-speed bins each hold 25.0 % of timepoints globally.
- [ ] Reward-available trials = 4,446 (11.7 %), all in the 28 task sessions from 5 mice.
- [ ] Stimulus id distribution matches the counts computed from raw `WallName` + `stim_id`.
- [ ] Spot-check `neural[s][t][n, k]` against a fresh `np.load` of the spk file.
- [ ] `time_to_sound_cue` crosses 0 at the frame nearest `SoundFr`.

---

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Convert the Zhong et al. 2025 ("Unsupervised pretraining in biological neural networks")
two-photon mesoscope dataset into the decoder-compatible pickle format.

Usage
-----
    python -u /app/convert_data.py <outpicklefile> [--full | --sample] [--show-processing]

Options
-------
    --full             process all 89 recordings (default)
    --sample           process only 2 recordings (for testing)
    --show-processing  save per-step diagnostic plots for up to 2 sessions as
                       processing_<session_id>.png

Pipeline (see CONVERSION_NOTES.md for the full rationale)
---------------------------------------------------------
1.  `Imaging_Exp_info.npy` -> 89 unique recordings (mouse, date, block).  The
    canonical stimulus id of every wall is merged over all experiment types in
    which the recording appears.
2.  Behaviour (`Beh_<exp_type>.npy`) -> per-frame masks and per-trial variables.
    Retained timepoints follow the reference recipe
    `fr_valid = (ft_move > 0) & ft_CorrSpc` (utils.Get_dprime_selective_neuron),
    i.e. inside the 0-4 m texture corridor while the VR (= the mouse) is moving.
3.  Neural data (`<rec>_neural_data.npy`) -> concatenated deconvolved traces,
    restricted to visual-cortex neurons (`iarea not in {-1, 7}`), subsampled to
    at most NNEURONS_KEEP per session (stratified over V1/mHV/lHV/aHV),
    z-scored per neuron, then split into trials.
"""

import argparse
import datetime
import os
import pickle
import sys
import time
from collections import defaultdict
from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor

import numpy as np

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Configuration
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT = '/app/data'
SPK_DIR = os.path.join(ROOT, 'spk')
BEH_DIR = os.path.join(ROOT, 'beh')
RET_DIR = os.path.join(ROOT, 'retinotopy')

# Neurons kept per session.  2000 == decoder.train_decoder's `svd_max_neurons` default,
# so the SVD initialisation uses the real neurons instead of a random Gaussian projection.
NNEURONS_KEEP = 2000
NEURON_SEED = 0

# Worker processes used to read the 405 GB of spk files (disk-bandwidth limited).
N_WORKERS = int(os.environ.get('CONVERT_WORKERS', '6'))

# Corridor geometry, in decimetres (beh['Texture_Length'] == 40, i.e. 4 m of texture).
CORRIDOR_DM = 40.0
N_POS_BINS = 4                       # 4 equal-length 1-m bins
POS_BIN_DM = CORRIDOR_DM / N_POS_BINS

N_SPEED_BINS = 4                     # quartiles of the pooled running-speed distribution

# Wall-clock time inputs are clipped to this many seconds (see CONVERSION_NOTES Step 5).
TIME_CLIP_S = 30.0

SEC_PER_DAY = 86400.0

BRAIN_REGIONS = ['V1', 'mHV', 'lHV', 'aHV']

# Canonical stimulus roles used throughout the reference code
# (utils.Get_coding_direction docstring / utils.get_cat_id).  Id 7 is added here for
# `circle3`, the only stimulus that never receives an id in Imaging_Exp_info.
STIM_NAMES = ['circle1', 'circle2', 'leaf1', 'leaf2', 'leaf3',
              'leaf1_swap1', 'leaf1_swap2', 'circle3']
STIM_EXTRA = {'circle3': 7}

INPUT_NAMES = ['time_to_sound_cue_s', 'day_of_training', 'time_since_trial_start_s',
               'reward_available']
OUTPUT_NAMES = ['stimulus', 'licking', 'position_bin', 'running_speed_bin']


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reference helpers (copied from /app/code/utils.py)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def neu_area_ID(iarea):
    """utils.neu_area_ID -- map retinotopy area codes onto the four visual areas."""
    idx = {}
    for ar in BRAIN_REGIONS:
        if ar == 'V1':
            idx[ar] = iarea == 8
        elif ar == 'mHV':
            idx[ar] = (iarea == 0) | (iarea == 1) | (iarea == 2) | (iarea == 9)
        elif ar == 'lHV':
            idx[ar] = (iarea == 5) | (iarea == 6)
        elif ar == 'aHV':
            idx[ar] = (iarea == 3) | (iarea == 4)
    return idx


def load_spk_planes(mname, datexp, blk):
    """utils.load_spk, but returning the individual plane arrays (avoids one full copy)."""
    fn = '%s_%s_%s_neural_data.npy' % (mname, datexp, blk)
    return np.load(os.path.join(SPK_DIR, fn), allow_pickle=True).item()['spks']


def load_iarea(mname, datexp):
    """utils.load_retino, but only the area code of each neuron."""
    d = np.load(os.path.join(RET_DIR, '%s_%s_trans.npz' % (mname, datexp)), allow_pickle=True)
    return d['iarea']


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 1: recording table
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def build_recording_table():
    """Return an ordered list of the 89 unique recordings with their merged stimulus map."""
    exp_info = np.load(os.path.join(BEH_DIR, 'Imaging_Exp_info.npy'), allow_pickle=True).item()

    recs = {}
    for exp_type, dbs in exp_info.items():
        for db in dbs:
            key = '%s_%s_%s' % (db['mname'], db['datexp'], db['blk'])
            behkey = key + '_' + db['stimtype'] if 'stimtype' in db else key
            if key not in recs:
                recs[key] = {
                    'key': key, 'mname': db['mname'], 'datexp': db['datexp'],
                    'blk': db['blk'], 'exp_types': [], 'beh_source': (exp_type, behkey),
                    'stim_map': {}, 'exptype': db.get('exptype', None),
                }
            r = recs[key]
            r['exp_types'].append(exp_type)
            if r['exptype'] is None and db.get('exptype') is not None:
                r['exptype'] = db['exptype']
            # merge the canonical stimulus ids contributed by this experiment type
            uniq = exp_info[exp_type][list(dbs).index(db)] if False else db
            for wall, sid in zip(_uniq_walls_placeholder(), []):
                pass
            r['_db_list'] = r.get('_db_list', []) + [(exp_type, behkey, db)]

    # "cohort" label: mice that were never given water are naive/unsupervised
    for r in recs.values():
        if r['exptype'] is None:
            r['exptype'] = 'naive'

    # day of training = days since that mouse's first recording
    by_mouse = defaultdict(list)
    for r in recs.values():
        by_mouse[r['mname']].append(r)
    for mname, rs in by_mouse.items():
        d0 = min(datetime.date(*map(int, r['datexp'].split('_'))) for r in rs)
        for r in rs:
            r['day'] = (datetime.date(*map(int, r['datexp'].split('_'))) - d0).days

    order = sorted(recs.values(), key=lambda r: (r['mname'], r['datexp'], r['blk']))
    return order, exp_info


def _uniq_walls_placeholder():
    return []


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 2: behaviour
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def load_behaviour(recs, verbose=True):
    """Fill each recording dict with the per-frame / per-trial behaviour it needs.

    Every Beh_<exp_type>.npy is read exactly once.  The stimulus map is merged over all
    experiment types; the behaviour arrays themselves are taken from the first experiment
    type containing the recording (they are identical across experiment types -- asserted).
    """
    by_key = {r['key']: r for r in recs}
    exp_types = sorted({et for r in recs for et in r['exp_types']})

    for exp_type in exp_types:
        t0 = time.time()
        B = np.load(os.path.join(BEH_DIR, 'Beh_' + exp_type + '.npy'), allow_pickle=True).item()
        for r in recs:
            for (et, behkey, db) in r['_db_list']:
                if et != exp_type:
                    continue
                beh = B[behkey]
                # merge canonical stimulus ids
                for wall, sid in zip(beh['UniqWalls'], db['stim_id']):
                    if not np.isnan(sid):
                        wall = str(wall)
                        prev = r['stim_map'].get(wall)
                        assert prev is None or prev == int(sid), \
                            'stim_id conflict %s %s: %s vs %s' % (r['key'], wall, prev, sid)
                        r['stim_map'][wall] = int(sid)
                if 'beh' not in r:
                    r['beh'] = _extract_beh(beh)
                else:
                    assert r['beh']['ntrials'] == int(beh['ntrials']), \
                        'behaviour mismatch across experiment types for %s' % r['key']
        del B
        if verbose:
            print('  loaded Beh_%s.npy (%.1fs)' % (exp_type, time.time() - t0), flush=True)
    return recs


def _extract_beh(beh):
    """Keep only the behaviour fields required by the conversion (small arrays)."""
    return {
        'ntrials': int(beh['ntrials']),
        'ft': np.asarray(beh['ft'], dtype=np.float64),
        'ft_trInd': np.asarray(beh['ft_trInd'], dtype=np.float64),
        'ft_move': np.asarray(beh['ft_move'], dtype=np.float64),
        'ft_CorrSpc': np.asarray(beh['ft_CorrSpc'], dtype=bool),
        'ft_Pos': np.asarray(beh['ft_Pos'], dtype=np.float64),
        'ft_RunSpeed': np.asarray(beh['ft_RunSpeed'], dtype=np.float64),
        'Trial_start_time': np.asarray(beh['Trial_start_time'], dtype=np.float64),
        'SoundTime': np.asarray(beh['SoundTime'], dtype=np.float64),
        'SoundFr': np.asarray(beh['SoundFr'], dtype=np.float64),
        'LickFr': np.asarray(beh['LickFr'], dtype=np.float64),
        'WallName': np.array([str(w) for w in beh['WallName']]),
        'isRew': np.asarray(beh['isRew'], dtype=bool),
        'Corridor_Length': float(beh['Corridor_Length']),
        'Texture_Length': float(beh['Texture_Length']),
    }


def compute_frame_selection(rec, nfr):
    """Reference recipe: inside the texture corridor AND the VR (mouse) is moving.

    utils.Get_dprime_selective_neuron:
        VRmove = beh['ft_move'][:nfr] > 0
        isCorridor = beh['ft_CorrSpc'][:nfr]
        fr_valid = VRmove & isCorridor
    plus a valid trial index (frames outside the behaviour have ft_trInd == NaN).
    """
    b = rec['beh']
    tr = b['ft_trInd'][:nfr]
    keep = (b['ft_move'][:nfr] > 0) & b['ft_CorrSpc'][:nfr] & ~np.isnan(tr)
    return keep


def build_trial_variables(rec, nfr, keep, speed_edges):
    """Build per-trial input/output arrays for the retained frames of one recording."""
    b = rec['beh']
    idx = np.flatnonzero(keep)                      # frame indices, ascending
    tri = b['ft_trInd'][idx].astype(np.int64)       # trial index of each retained frame
    ft = b['ft'][idx]

    # ---- per-trial scalars -----------------------------------------------------------
    ntr = b['ntrials']
    wall = b['WallName']
    stim_id = np.array([rec['stim_map'].get(w, STIM_EXTRA.get(w, -1)) for w in wall],
                       dtype=np.int64)
    assert (stim_id >= 0).all(), 'unmapped stimulus in %s: %s' % (
        rec['key'], sorted(set(wall[stim_id < 0])))

    if b['isRew'].any():
        rew_stim = wall[b['isRew']][0]              # utils.get_cat_id
        rew_avail = (wall == rew_stim).astype(np.float32)
    else:
        rew_avail = np.zeros(ntr, dtype=np.float32)

    # ---- time-varying variables ------------------------------------------------------
    t_since_start = (ft - b['Trial_start_time'][tri]) * SEC_PER_DAY
    t_to_cue = (b['SoundTime'][tri] - ft) * SEC_PER_DAY
    t_since_start = np.clip(t_since_start, 0.0, TIME_CLIP_S)
    t_to_cue = np.clip(t_to_cue, -TIME_CLIP_S, TIME_CLIP_S)

    pos = b['ft_Pos'][idx]
    pos_bin = np.clip((pos / POS_BIN_DM).astype(np.int64), 0, N_POS_BINS - 1)

    speed = b['ft_RunSpeed'][idx]
    speed_bin = np.searchsorted(speed_edges, speed, side='right').astype(np.int64)
    speed_bin = np.clip(speed_bin, 0, N_SPEED_BINS - 1)

    # licking: the reference indexes event frames with `.astype(int)` (floor)
    lick_fr = b['LickFr']
    lick_fr = lick_fr[np.isfinite(lick_fr)]
    lick_fr = lick_fr[(lick_fr >= 0) & (lick_fr < nfr)].astype(np.int64)
    lick_frame = np.zeros(nfr, dtype=bool)
    lick_frame[lick_fr] = True
    licking = lick_frame[idx].astype(np.int64)

    # ---- split into trials -----------------------------------------------------------
    # trial boundaries: retained frames are sorted, and ft_trInd is non-decreasing on them
    assert np.all(np.diff(tri) >= 0), 'trial indices not monotonic for %s' % rec['key']
    bounds = np.flatnonzero(np.diff(tri)) + 1
    starts = np.concatenate(([0], bounds))
    stops = np.concatenate((bounds, [len(tri)]))
    trial_ids = tri[starts]

    inputs, outputs, slices = [], [], []
    for s, e, t in zip(starts, stops, trial_ids):
        T = e - s
        inp = np.empty((4, T), dtype=np.float32)
        inp[0] = t_to_cue[s:e]
        inp[1] = rec['day']
        inp[2] = t_since_start[s:e]
        inp[3] = rew_avail[t]
        out = np.empty((4, T), dtype=np.int64)
        out[0] = stim_id[t]
        out[1] = licking[s:e]
        out[2] = pos_bin[s:e]
        out[3] = speed_bin[s:e]
        inputs.append(inp)
        outputs.append(out)
        slices.append((s, e))

    diag = {'idx': idx, 'tri': tri, 'pos': pos, 'speed': speed, 'licking': licking,
            't_since_start': t_since_start, 't_to_cue': t_to_cue,
            'pos_bin': pos_bin, 'speed_bin': speed_bin, 'trial_ids': trial_ids,
            'starts': starts, 'stops': stops, 'stim_id': stim_id, 'rew_avail': rew_avail}
    return inputs, outputs, trial_ids, slices, diag


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 3: neural data (runs in worker processes)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def select_neurons(iarea, n_keep, seed):
    """Visual-cortex neurons only, stratified-random subsample over the four areas.

    Returns (global neuron indices, brain_region_idx) sorted by neuron index.
    """
    area_idx = neu_area_ID(iarea)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)

    per_area = [np.flatnonzero(area_idx[ar]) for ar in BRAIN_REGIONS]
    n_vis = sum(len(a) for a in per_area)
    if n_vis <= n_keep:
        chosen = [a for a in per_area]
    else:
        # proportional allocation with largest-remainder rounding
        exact = np.array([len(a) for a in per_area], dtype=np.float64) / n_vis * n_keep
        take = np.floor(exact).astype(int)
        rem = n_keep - take.sum()
        if rem > 0:
            order = np.argsort(-(exact - take))
            take[order[:rem]] += 1
        take = np.minimum(take, [len(a) for a in per_area])
        chosen = [rng.choice(a, size=k, replace=False) if k < len(a) else a
                  for a, k in zip(per_area, take)]

    idx = np.concatenate(chosen) if len(chosen) else np.zeros(0, dtype=np.int64)
    region = np.concatenate([np.full(len(c), i, dtype=np.int64)
                             for i, c in enumerate(chosen)]) if len(chosen) else \
        np.zeros(0, dtype=np.int64)
    order = np.argsort(idx)
    return idx[order].astype(np.int64), region[order].astype(np.int64)


def process_neural(task):
    """Worker: load one recording's spk file and return the per-trial neural matrices."""
    t0 = time.time()
    key = task['key']
    planes = load_spk_planes(task['mname'], task['datexp'], task['blk'])
    nfr = planes[0].shape[1]
    n_total = sum(p.shape[0] for p in planes)
    t_load = time.time() - t0

    iarea = task['iarea']
    assert len(iarea) == n_total, \
        '%s: retinotopy has %d neurons, spk has %d' % (key, len(iarea), n_total)

    keep = task['keep_fn'](nfr)
    keep_idx = np.flatnonzero(keep)

    neu_idx, region = select_neurons(iarea, task['n_keep'], task['seed'])

    # gather the selected rows / retained columns plane by plane
    offs = np.cumsum([0] + [p.shape[0] for p in planes])
    blocks = []
    for pi, p in enumerate(planes):
        lo, hi = offs[pi], offs[pi + 1]
        sel = neu_idx[(neu_idx >= lo) & (neu_idx < hi)] - lo
        if len(sel) == 0:
            continue
        blocks.append(p[sel][:, keep_idx])
    X = np.concatenate(blocks, axis=0).astype(np.float32) if blocks else \
        np.zeros((0, len(keep_idx)), np.float32)
    del planes, blocks

    raw_stats = {'mean': float(X.mean()) if X.size else 0.0,
                 'max': float(X.max()) if X.size else 0.0}

    # z-score each neuron over the retained timepoints of this session
    mu = X.mean(axis=1, keepdims=True)
    sd = X.std(axis=1, keepdims=True)
    n_dead = int((sd[:, 0] == 0).sum())
    sd[sd == 0] = 1.0
    X -= mu
    X /= sd

    trials = [np.ascontiguousarray(X[:, s:e]) for (s, e) in task['slices']]
    return {
        'key': key, 'trials': trials, 'brain_region_idx': region,
        'n_total_neurons': int(n_total), 'n_visual_neurons': int((iarea != -1).sum() -
                                                                 (iarea == 7).sum()),
        'n_kept_neurons': int(len(neu_idx)), 'n_dead': n_dead, 'nfr': int(nfr),
        'raw_stats': raw_stats, 't_load': t_load, 't_total': time.time() - t0,
    }


class _KeepFn:
    """Picklable closure computing the retained-frame mask once nfr is known."""

    def __init__(self, ft_move, ft_CorrSpc, ft_trInd):
        self.ft_move, self.ft_CorrSpc, self.ft_trInd = ft_move, ft_CorrSpc, ft_trInd

    def __call__(self, nfr):
        tr = self.ft_trInd[:nfr]
        return (self.ft_move[:nfr] > 0) & self.ft_CorrSpc[:nfr] & ~np.isnan(tr)

def plot_processing(rec, diag, neural_trials, nfr, speed_edges, outdir='/app'):

    for ed in speed_edges:
        ax.axhline(ed, color='b', ls=':', lw=0.8)

    ax.set_title('running speed, dotted = global quartile edges')

    # (1,0) position -> position bin
    ax = axes[1, 0]
    ax.plot(diag['pos'], diag['pos_bin'], 'k.', ms=1)

    ax.set_title('position discretisation (4 x 1 m)')

    # (1,1) speed -> speed bin

    ax.set_title('speed discretisation, session fractions = %s' %
